records.name: Kingsessing Recreation Center
records.notes: City recreation center run by Philadelphia Parks and Recreation. It was rebuilt and reopened in March 2026 (the city release is headed March 20, 2026). Billy Penn gives the address as 4901 Kingsessing Ave (2022); 2017 coverage says 5001. This is a city building, not a community group, so it is not published. Its advisory council is listed in leads_only. The Inquirer (Oct 6, 2023) says Councilmember Jamie Gauthier's district includes the center, so check whether it falls inside Council District 2.

records.name: Eastwick: From Recovery to Resilience
records.notes: City Office of Sustainability program that holds resident meetings on flood mitigation and neighborhood updates. The newest dated item found is a meeting slide deck whose date reads 26 Mas 2026 (the page uses a translated month name, probably March). The program page links a newsletter sign-up, lists eastwick@phila.gov and a phone number, and names no partner groups. It is a city initiative, not a community group, so it is not published. If the owner wants city programs in the directory, this is the candidate.

leads_only.name: Eastwick United CDC
leads_only.note: Named as an organizer of the Eastwick Community Day on June 29, 2024, on a city page. No website was linked or found in this run, so not checked.

leads_only.name: Eastwick Friends and Neighbors Coalition
leads_only.note: Named as an attendee at the June 29, 2024 Eastwick Community Day on a city page. No website or contact found, so not checked.

leads_only.name: Eastwick Community Garden Association
leads_only.note: Runs the Eastwick Community Garden at Bartram and Island Avenues. The newest dated mention is a July 8, 2021 PHL article, so it is dormant by the date rule. No website found. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Kingsessing Recreation Advisory Council
leads_only.note: Advisory council for the Kingsessing Recreation Center, led by Constance Crews, called its president in the Oct 6, 2023 Inquirer article. Billy Penn (2022) names Antoinette Holliday as secretary. The newest dated mention is Oct 2023, so it is dormant by the date rule. No own page, and the March 2026 reopening coverage does not name it. Not checked for current activity.

leads_only.name: Friends of Kingsessing
leads_only.note: Volunteer program at the Kingsessing Recreation Center, first work day set for Feb 25, 2017. No dated activity found after 2017. A Facebook page was mentioned in 2017 and was not read (Facebook is lead only). Not checked further.

leads_only.name: Paschalville Branch Library Job Readiness Center
leads_only.note: Job readiness center based at the Paschalville Branch Library at 70th and Woodland, named in an Aug 22, 2016 photo essay. Operator and current status unknown. The Free Library site was blocked, so not checked.

leads_only.name: Bartram's Garden
leads_only.note: Named as a Southwest Philadelphia recreation asset in a June 15, 2016 WHYY article. Its own website was not found in this run and was not guessed. It may sit in or near Kingsessing south, so it is worth a future check.

leads_only.name: Fairmount Park Conservancy (Blue Bell Inn)
leads_only.note: Named in the 2016 photo essay as the operator linked to the Blue Bell Inn at Woodland Avenue and Cobbs Creek Parkway. Citywide conservancy, so it may sit outside this slice. Not checked.

notes: Thin lane: no publish records. All 6 WebSearch calls were used (hard cap) and 19 fetches were made. Only two records were written, both not_a_group (a city recreation center and a city program). The 20 to 40 target was not reachable: no group in this slice turned up with its own working website and dated activity in the last 24 months. Neighborhoods with nothing found: Elmwood Park, Paschall, Penrose and Clearview. The searches returned no civic association, friends group or advisory council for these four. Eastwick United CDC, Eastwick Friends and Neighbors Coalition, Eastwick Community Garden Association, Kingsessing Recreation Advisory Council and Friends of Kingsessing have no website linked from any page I could read, so they sit in leads_only. Bartram's Garden's site was not guessed. Not reached: Free Library branch pages (403), philadelphianeighborhoods.com (403), phlcouncil.com/district-2/ (404, path not valid), and the phila2035.org Lower Southwest district page (404). No rate limiting was seen, and 403 responses were not retried. Suggested next steps for a later run: find the City Planning Commission Registry of Community Organizations list for the Lower Southwest planning district (PCPC May 15, 2025 minutes say the RCO registration window ran June 1 to June 30; the list itself was not located); look for the Council District 2 office's own list of groups; check the Free Library Paschalville and Eastwick branch pages; and search for Elmwood, Penrose and Clearview civic groups or recreation advisory councils. Address conflict: the Kingsessing rec center is 4901 Kingsessing Ave in Billy Penn (2022) and 5001 in 2017 coverage. Council district: the Inquirer (Oct 2023) says Councilmember Jamie Gauthier's district includes the Kingsessing rec center; check whether it falls in Council District 2.
